opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee E014 (Andrew Mann) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin only for owners; write is within policy). Grant write access.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E014 (Andrew Mann) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend read. Note: this conflicts with HR note claiming full-time employee.
reason: The Security note reports that E014 (Andrew Mann) is a contractor with basic security training, which directly governs access: contractors are limited to read, or write only with advanced security training. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum for a contractor with basic training, the maximum of read should be granted. Note that this conflicts with the HR note claiming full-time status; however, the Security database explicitly flags this conflict and its data indicates contractor status, so I applied the more conservative, policy-compliant level.
